title: Pressure probe — weekly lab synthesis
body:
Goal: synthesize this week's pressure-probe lab runs across seq-limited and mixed workloads, surface consistent failure modes, and define a 48h triage plan. These notes are a terse capture of the runs, hypotheses, and concrete next steps.

Runs summary (dec 18–21):
- run-A (seq=512, batch-target=32, kv-cache=on): 6 replicates; median p50=78ms, p99=360ms; two replicates showed 2–3x p99 spikes at minutes 12–14.
- run-B (seq=128, bursty mix, batch-target=8, kv-cache=warm): sustained qps 1.8k; tail latency jitter correlated with GC-like host OOM events on node-3 (infra logs).
- run-C (mixed seq, enqueue-priority=high, cache-eviction-threshold lowered): saw throughput drop ~12% when queue depth exceeded 64 for >45s. No model change.

Observations:
1) Spike timing is consistent across different batches: most p99 spikes align to ~12–15min into the run. Pattern looks like a periodic background task (checkpoint/metric-flusher) colliding with peak batch assembly.
2) KV-cache churn hypothesis: when cache temperature rises (mixed-seq), we see more frequent cache misses which increases CPU work and magnifies tail latency under high queue depth.
3) Sidecar scheduling jitter: traces show sidecar preemption windows around the same time as spikes. On node-3 we observed higher steal time.
4) Queue depth interaction: lowering enqueue-priority smooths throughput but increases median slightly; suggests our batching heuristics are sensitive to burst alignment.

Quick reproduction commands (lab):
- repro harness: ./tools/run-pressure --profile mixed-seq --seq-dist=zipf --batch=8 --duration=20m --collect=traces,metrics
- cache warm script: scripts/warm-cache.sh --model=gptx-medium --prefixes=2000

Hypotheses (ranked):
A. Periodic infra job (checkpoint/metrics flush) causes short CPU throttling windows that amplify batching tail. (high priority)
B. KV-cache eviction churn increases per-request CPU work when cache miss rate >0.12, causing backlog pressure and p99 spikes. (medium)
C. Scheduler/sidecar interference on specific instance types (n1-highcpu-32 variant) produces higher steal and increases latency variance. (medium)

Immediate next steps (48h plan):
- (Aisha) Add a synthetic run w/ infra jobs disabled on a control node and compare p99 alignment (target: 12–24h).
- (Miguel) Instrument and pin a lightweight kernel-level trace (perf top snapshot at spike time) and upload to ENG-7891.
- (Jordan) Run cache-miss sweep varying eviction threshold from 0.05 to 0.20 and report miss->p99 slope.
- (Priya) Coordinate with infra to identify any automated cron jobs around 12–16m mark; collect host dmesg + systemd timers.

Longer runway items (next sprint):
- Batching heuristic experiment: decouple batch assembly window from enqueue priority and evaluate tail impact on mixed workloads.
- Explore token-level KV-cache hotkey detection and selective pinning to reduce churn for heavy prefixes.
- Consider a small runtime change to defer non-critical metric flushing outside of predictably hot windows.

Risks & open questions:
- If root cause is infra-level (cron/checkpoint), mitigation is operational, not product — but we need an automatic fallback (model variant route) to avoid customer-visible regressions.
- Are sidecar CPU budgets being set correctly for the newer host types? current limit: 0.15 CPU share in cgroup.

Attachments & artifacts: traces + flamegraphs for run-A replicates (uploaded to linked PR), run logs (S3: s3://redwood-lab/pressure/2026-12-21/), dashboard snapshots (links in ENG-7891).

Meeting ask for next sync (mon 2026-12-27):
- one page comparison: control vs candidate (A disabled infra job).
- short demo: perf top around spike showing top 5 symbols.
- decision: hold canary if p99 impact >2x baseline or run-time mitigation available.

Notes to self: capture exact wall-clock timestamps for the three spike windows next to host logs; avoid re-running on node-3 until infra cron is triaged.

TL;DR: Recurrent p99 spikes appear when background infra activity coincides with batch assembly under elevated cache churn. Immediate lab work is focused on isolating infra cron vs KV-cache churn. If isolation confirms infra, schedule operational windows; if cache, prioritize heuristic/eviction tuning.
